subject.title: Manage Claw cron jobs through the gateway

question: Should canonical `agents.delete` adopt a durable cross-store cron-teardown contract in this Claws stack, and must that contract land before any scheduler jobs are removed automatically?
rationale: This changes established agent-deletion behavior, introduces persistent shared state, and chooses failure semantics across the non-transactional scheduler/config boundary; tests cannot determine the intended compatibility contract.

options.title: Require durable deletion first
options.body: Keep the PR open until canonical deletion persists resumable teardown state, covers config failure after remote removal, and has running-Gateway proof.

options.title: Narrow to Claw ownership
options.body: Remove the global `agents.delete` behavior from this slice and keep cron cleanup limited to explicitly tracked Claw ownership until a separate canonical-deletion design lands.

options.title: Pause for the RFC stack
options.body: Hold this PR until the Claws RFC and preceding export/lifecycle slices establish the permanent ownership and deletion contracts.

recommendation.title: Require durable deletion first
recommendation.body: Keep the PR open until canonical deletion persists resumable teardown state, covers config failure after remote removal, and has running-Gateway proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the concrete failure reproductions and articulated the canonical deletion boundary this PR is attempting to implement.
